To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) complex event extraction from biomedical text can be approached with a pipeline of machine learning algorithms; and 2) rich graph-based features are useful for this task.

1) complex events are better represented by a nested graph structure than by a flat list; 2) a wide variety of rich graph-based features are useful; 3) the task can be divided into independent steps that can be solved with machine learning; and 4) the performance of the best system can be improved by post-processing.

(1) a machine learning approach to event extraction can be successfully applied, (2) a wide array of graph-based features can be extracted from dependency parse graphs, and (3) a rule-based post-processing is an effective way to refine the output.
